previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, epilepsy, and cardiomyopathy, was admitted after becoming altered during dialysis, prompting a stroke alert. He had a witnessed seizure in the CT scanner and tested positive for influenza A. Brain imaging showed no acute stroke or hemorrhage. He was treated with oseltamivir and had his anti-seizure medications adjusted, including increased levetiracetam and continued oxcarbazepine with post-dialysis dosing. He remained seizure-free, returned to baseline mental status, and completed dialysis. Discharge was to an extended care facility with follow-up plans for thyroid ultrasound, dental evaluation, and monitoring of a small pulmonary nodule.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  History: ___ with fever, hypoxemia, recent flu// eval for PNA

TECHNIQUE:  Chest PA and lateral

COMPARISON:  Chest radiographs from ___.

FINDINGS: 

Frontal and lateral chest radiographs demonstrate a left subclavian line with
the catheter terminating in the upper right atrium.  There are low lung
volumes, exaggerating cardiac size and bronchovascular crowding.  Heart size
is mildly enlarged.  Asymmetrically increased opacity in the right lung is due
to a combination persistent mild asymmetric pulmonary edema and right lower
lobe pneumonia.

IMPRESSION: 

Persistent mild asymmetric pulmonary edema and right lower lobe pneumonia.

EXAMINATION:  CHEST (PORTABLE AP)

INDICATION:  History: ___ with pneumonia// eval for falsh

TECHNIQUE:  Upright AP view of the chest

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph ___ at 06:36: ___

FINDINGS: 

Assessment of the chest is slightly limited by patient rotation.  Left-sided
dual lumen central venous catheter coursing through a left brachiocephalic and
SVC stent terminates in the proximal right atrium, unchanged.  Multiple clips
are again noted within the superior paramediastinal region palpable with prior
thyroid surgery.  Left superior mediastinal mass compatible with known
multinodular thyroid goiter with similar rightward deviation of the trachea is
re-demonstrated.  Moderate to severe cardiac enlargement persists. 
Ill-defined airspace opacification within the right lung is similar compared
to the prior exam, and likely reflects a combination of asymmetric pulmonary
edema and pneumonia, not substantially changed in the interval.  A trace right
pleural effusion is present.  No pneumothorax is identified.  Vascular stent
in the left axillary region is unchanged.

IMPRESSION: 

No substantial interval change and asymmetric airspace opacification in the
right lung, likely a combination of asymmetric pulmonary edema and pneumonia.
